subject: Recap & next steps: MedAvant model-fit benchmarks, dataset format, and scoring
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alison Tucker <alison.tucker@medavant.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: MedAvant model-fit benchmarks, dataset format, and scoring

Hi Alison — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for the pilot eval run on Redwood.

Call highlights (minutes):
- Goal: validate model fit for triage summarization and coding assist across a 5k-case seed dataset; measure accuracy, hallucination rate, and latency under 1s/token SLO.
- Priority outputs: entity extraction F1, summary ROUGE-L, and a binary hallucination signal (human-labeled).
- Compliance: MedAvant will supply de-identified extracts (see format suggestions below).

Redwood recommended models (starting point):
- small-latency baseline: redwood-llama-13B-q4f (fast, lower cost)
- quality candidate: redwood-mistral-34b-instruct (higher-quality; track cost delta)
- fallback for throughput tests: redwood-qlora-7B (cheap burst capacity)

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) You share a 500–1,000 row sample (anonymized) in CSV with the column schema in the template I attached.
2) Marissa will prepare a scoring rubric + the prompt set we used in today’s demo and a runnable scoring script.
3) We run an initial 1k-run on Redwood Dedicated and share the bench report (latency, token-cost, and scorer outputs) within 3 business days of data receipt.
4) Review call to go over results and decide whether to expand to 5k.

Attachments: medavant_eval_template.csv (CSV schema + sample), prompt_sets_v1.txt (demo prompts), sow-draft.docx (SOW skeleton).

Please confirm timeline from your side and whether you need a signed DPA before we ingest samples.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0119

--
Note: we will only ingest samples to a customer-scoped bucket with KMS key and no full PHI — happy to share our data handling checklist if you want it now.

From: Alison Tucker <alison.tucker@medavant.com>

Cc: Kevin Price <kevin.price@medavant.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: MedAvant model-fit benchmarks, dataset format, and scoring

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and questions:

-We can provide a 750-row anonymized sample by end of day Monday. We'll remove direct identifiers and token-shred dates per our internal policy.
-Question on labels: for hallucination we plan to include a binary column ("human_hallucination") plus an optional free-text rationale. Is that compatible with your scoring script?
-Do you require a specific hash salt or pseudonymization method? We usually use SHA-256 with a staff-supplied salt.
-Can the initial run be on a Hosted API key or do you recommend Dedicated for repeatability?

Also Kevin (cc'd) will be our technical lead on this — he may want to join the first setup call with Marissa.

Thanks,
Alison Tucker
Head of Clinical Innovation | MedAvant Health
alison.tucker@medavant.com | (617) 555-2082

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alison Tucker <alison.tucker@medavant.com>, Kevin Price <kevin.price@medavant.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: MedAvant model-fit benchmarks, dataset format, and scoring

Hi Alison / Kevin — happy to take point on the technical setup. A few specifics to make your sample ingestion and our scoring run smoother:

Dataset format (per attached template):
- file: medavant_eval_template.csv (UTF-8, comma-delimited)
- required columns: case_id, encounter_date_utc, source_text, gold_summary, human_hallucination (0/1), human_labeler_id (hashed)
- optional columns: coding_hint, severity_bucket
- max row size: 50KB per source_text (we can chunk if needed)
- sample: 750 rows OK; file size < 250MB preferred for upload to S3.

Pseudonymization & hashing:
- SHA-256 with your salt is fine — include the salt separately via secure channel; we do not store salts.
- If you prefer, we can provide a short script to run client-side to produce hashed labeler IDs.

Scoring & thresholds (what we'll run):
- Entity extraction: micro F1 (span overlap tolerance = 0.5)
- Summary: ROUGE-L and a BERTScore pass at precision >= 0.85 as a quality gate
- Hallucination: compare model outputs vs gold_summary and human_hallucination; we compute a precision/recall on hallucination flags and surface examples for manual review.
- Latency/cost: median p50 token latency and tokens/second across each model variant.

Prompts and reproducibility:
- prompt_sets_v1.txt includes the initial instruction templates we demoed. We also keep a canonical prompt hash so reruns can validate prompt drift.
- We'll check for prompt-template-sensitive regressions by computing per-prompt-case delta between models.

Run environment recommendation:
- For the initial 1k diagnostic run: Hosted API is fine for speed but Dedicated gives repeatable latency and stable KV cache for multi-shot evaluation. If you care about strict SLO comparisons, use Dedicated; otherwise Hosted is acceptable.

Uploads & links:
- Upload sample to the S3 path: s3://redwood-inference/benchmarks/medavant/staging/ (we will create a customer-scoped prefix after you confirm).
- Shared drive with scoring notebook and example outputs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleMedAvantBenchmarks

I attached a stubbed scoring script and the CSV template to this thread. Let me know a good window for a 30m setup call — I have availability Monday 10:00–12:00 and Tuesday 14:00–16:00 PT.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0193

Attachments: medavant_eval_template.csv (CSV schema + sample), prompt_sets_v1.txt (prompts + examples)
